newsitem.title: YUGOSLAVIA: Yugo Jan-Sept raw steel output 422,493 T - report.
newsitem.headline: Yugo Jan-Sept raw steel output 422,493 T - report.

text.p: Production of raw steel in the Smederevo and Niksic works rose to 422,493 tonnes from January to September, tripling output in the same period last year, the Ferrous Metallurgy Association of Yugoslavia said in its latest report.
Smederevo's output stood at 331,350 tonnes, up by 269,172 tonnes on last year, while Niksic output rose by 21,898 tonnes to 91,143 tonnes.
In the same period, Smederevo, Niksic and other steel processing plants produced 454,985 tonnes of finished steel products, of which 245,803 tonnes were marketed locally.
In comparison, 1995's January-September output of finished steel products stood at 176,555 tonnes of which 172,347 was marketed locally.
Since April, when the biggest steel works in Smederevo restarted, production has stabilised at a level several times higher than in the past three years.
The Smederevo works is expected to produce some 550,000 and Niksic around 120,000 tonnes of steel in 1996.

"This year, more than 650,000 tonnes of finished steel products will be offered to the local and foreign markets, which is 2.6 times more than in 1995," said Arsenije Jovanovic, director of the ferrous metallurgy association.

With output of finished steel products expected to reach nearly one million tonnes next year, far exceeding domestic demand, Yugoslav steel producers will have to export around 60 percent of their output, Jovanovic said.
Total imports of steel products in the January-September period surged by 45 percent against the same period last year to reach 162,699 tonnes.

A five-fold rise in exports to 125,333 tonnes compared to the same period in 1995 was attributed to the suspension of international sanctions against rump Yugoslavia, comprising Serbia and Montenegro, in November last year. -- Amra Kevic, Belgrade newsroom +381 11 2224305
